DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http://wwrvv.dilq.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 69 s. 2021 5 May 2021 HON. RUBEN UY DIOKNO Mayor Municipality of Padre Burgos Province of Quezon Dear Mayor Diokno: This has reference to the electronic mail of Mrs. Carmelita Cayabyab, 72 years old, a resident of Concepcion Uno, Marikina City, born in the Municipality of Padre Burgos, Province of Quezon, and was married to her late husband in the same Municipality. According to Mrs. Cayabyab, she is processing the transfer of his late husband's pension to her name. Based on the assessment of PNP Retirement and Benefits Administration Service (PRBS)-Crame, the spelling of her late husband's name in the latter's Certificate of No Marriage (CENOMAR) is wrong. For said reason, she was advised to process the CENOMAR correction where they celebrated their marriage. Thereafter, she proceeded to Padre Burgos, Quezon on 09 January 2020 to process the correction, but to no avail. Allegedly, she was told by a staff member of the Municipal Registry Office that since 2019, after the election, you have not yet appointed a Municipal Civil Registrar, and that for said reason, all papers forwarded to Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) were returned to the Municipal Civil Registry of Padre Burgos citing that the signatory was merely an Officer-in-charge (OIC). Further, according to Mrs. Cayabyab, she again communicated with the Municipality of Padre Burgos, wherein she was informed that the documents pertinent to the request for correction were already forwarded to PSA. However, she was told that said documents will only be returned by PSA since the signatory was merely an OIC. Moreover, a staff member told her that you did appoint a Municipal Civil Registrar but was allegedly disapproved by the Civil Service Commission for being unqualified.

Under this premise arose the request for assistance pertaining to your action, and/or proper course of action that must be undertaken relative to Ms. Cayabyab's request for assistance on this matter. At the outset, this Department would like to stress that under Section 78 of Republic Act No. 7160 otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991" (LGC), it provides that all matters pertinent to human resources and development in local government units shall be governed by the civil service law and such rules and regulations and other issuances promulgated pursuant thereto, unless otherwise specified in this Code. In that regard, we shall discuss only the provisions of law or rules which we deem applicable based on the representations in the letter. Be that as it may, this Department would like to stress the pertinent provisions of the LGC in relation to municipal officials in general, to wit SECTION 443. Officials of the Municipal Government. — (a) a mayor, a municipal vice-mayor, sangguniang bayan members, a secretary to the sangguniang bayan, a municipal treasurer, a municipal assessor, a municipal accountant, a municipal budget officer, a municipal planning and development coordinator, a municipal engineer/building official, a municipal health officer and a municipal civil reqistrar. SECTION 479. Qualifications, Powers and Duties. - (a) No person shall be appointed civil registrar unless he is a citizen of the Philippines, a resident of the local government unit concerned, of good moral character, a holder of a college degree from a recognized college or university, and a first grade civil service eligible or its equivalent. He must have acquired experience in civil registry work for at least five (5) years in the case of the city civil registrar and three (3) years in the case of the municipal civil registrar. The appointment of a civil registrar for city and municipal governments. The afore-quoted provisions, explicitly provide that each municipality must have a municipal civil registrar, which refers to the head of the local civil registry office of the municipality, and the law states that such appointment is mandatory. Furthermore, as provided in Section 444(b)(1 )(v), one of the duties of a municipal mayor is to appoint all officials and employees whose salaries and wages are wholly or mainly paid out of municipal funds and

whose appointments are not otherwise provided for in this Code, as well as those he may be authorized by law to appoint. Correspondingly, a mere Officer-in-Charge(OlC) would not suffice as to what the law requires for the reason that an OIC enjoys limited powers which are confined to the functions of administration and ensuring that the office continues its usual activities, and does not involve the exercise of discretion. Hence, so long as an individual possesses all the qualification and none of the disqualifications, he or she may be appointed as a municipal civil registrar. Further, it is noteworthy to highlight Section 27(2) of Chapter V, Book V of Executive Order No. 292, otherwise known as the "Administrative Code of 1987: (2) Temporary appointment.—ln the absence of appropriate eligibles and it becomes necessarv in the public interest to fill a vacancy. a temporary appointment shall be issued to a person who meets all the requirements for the position to which he is being appointed except the appropriate civil service eligibility: Provided, That such temporary appointment shall not exceed twelve months, but the appointee may be replaced sooner if a qualified civil service eligible becomes available. Notwithstanding the situation, wherein there is an absence of appropriate eligible, and it becomes necessary in the public interest to fill a vacancy, an appointment under a temporary status may still be issued to a person who meets all the qualification requirements of the position except eligibility. Hence, by virtue of this Department's power of general supervision over local government units and its officials, you are hereby enjoined to appoint a civil registrar as mandated by the LGC, considering that the absence of a duly appointed Municipal Registrar will adversely affect the provision of services to your constituents as in the case of Mrs Carmelita Cayabyab Please be guided accordingly.

Very truly yours, BYA HORITY OF THE SECRETARY: ret a GAN for Local Government LLLS/32 COPY FURNISHED: DIR. ARIEL O. IGLESIA CESO IV-A (CALABARZON) Regional Director 3/F Andenson Bldg. 1, National Highway, Brgy. Parian, City of Calamba, Laguna 4027, Manila S Rd, Calamba, 4027 Laguna MRS. CARMELITA PUBLICO CAYABYAB Concepcion Uno, Marikina City : DILG :
